learning_outcomes.text: Know the main data preprocessing techniques and determine the most appropriate in each context.
Perform a principal component analysis and know the main methods.
Perform an exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis of a dataset.
Know the different multidimensional scaling methods and the differences between them.
Perform a correspondence analysis on a dataset.
Fluently handle the different concepts and methodologies within discriminant analysis.
Distinguish appropriately between all the previous techniques and apply the adequate one in each context.

syllabus_topics: Data preprocessing techniques. Motivation. Preprocessing tasks: cleaning, integration, transformation, reduction and discretization of data.
Principal component analysis. Correlation-based method. Covariance-based method. Limitations.
Multidimensional scaling (MDS). Classic and non-metric models.
Discriminant analysis. Discriminant functions. LDA, incremental LDA, multiclass LDA and high-dimensional LDA methods.

assessment_methods.method: Participation in forums and Campus Virtual activities

assessment_rules: The final grade for the ordinary call is calculated using the formula: Final grade = 0.05·A + 0.10·T + 0.40·P + 0.45·E. A minimum final grade of 5 out of 10 is required to pass the subject. For the extraordinary call in July, students can retain the grades obtained in the ordinary call. For the extraordinary call in January, the evaluation will consist of a theoretical-practical final exam, which will constitute 100% of the final grade. In all cases, a minimum of 5 out of 10 is required to pass.
